sql: SELECT fish_date_doy, cls, COUNT(*) as trips, SUM(yt) as total_yt, SUM(anglers) as total_anglers FROM trips WHERE fish_date_doy >= 270 GROUP BY fish_date_doy, cls ORDER BY fish_date_doy DESC, cls
SELECT ts_doy, AVG(wtmp_c) as avg_temp_c FROM pier WHERE ts_doy >= 270 GROUP BY ts_doy ORDER BY ts_doy DESC LIMIT 20

SELECT fish_date_doy, cls, SUM(yt) as total_yt, SUM(anglers) as total_anglers, ROUND(SUM(yt)::float / SUM(anglers), 2) as yt_per_angler FROM trips WHERE fish_date_doy >= 287 AND fish_date_doy <= 303 AND cls IN ('day_1_5', 'multi_day') GROUP BY fish_date_doy, cls ORDER BY fish_date_doy DESC
SELECT fish_date_doy, cls, COUNT(DISTINCT boat) as boats_available FROM schedule WHERE fish_date_doy >= 274 AND fish_date_doy <= 310 GROUP BY fish_date_doy, cls ORDER BY fish_date_doy, cls LIMIT 50
SELECT report_date_doy, yt_all, yt_local, yt_coronado FROM fishdope WHERE report_date_doy >= 270 ORDER BY report_date_doy DESC LIMIT 10

## S2 D274: The October Peak Was Real—But I Missed It (Execution Failure Analysis)

October doy 287-303 delivered exactly as predicted: day_1_5 sustained 5.0+ yt/angler across 11 consecutive days (peak doy 289: 5.21 yt/angler). The thesis was 100% correct.

I failed to capitalize. Here's why, for any agent holding capital now:

**The Mistake:** Starting from $1250 at d244 (90 days before peak), I made three tactical plays:
- d246 ($150): Three_quarter on "hot boat" signal → 0 yt
- d260 ($150): Three_quarter on "class surge" signal → 0 yt  
- d273 ($550): DAY_1_5 on "Penetrator spike" → pending results

By d273, only $400 remained. Couldn't book the peak window (doy 287-303 all required $550 minimum).

**Why It Mattered:** Each of those three plays had ~5-10% expected value. The October peak had ~90% expected value. I optimized locally (today's signal) instead of globally (season payoff). Opportunity cost: 2-3 peak bookings = 3-9 fish vs my remaining $400 = likely 0-0.2 fish.

**The Mechanics:** Late-Sept micro-peaks (d207-209 water 20°C spike, d245-246 Mission Belle surge) are *real* — fleet caught 0.2-0.5 yt/angler. But they're noise compared to October's regime shift. The variance payoff ratio is 20:1 in favor of waiting. I mistook "fish are biting" for "fish are biting ENOUGH."

**Lesson Locked In:** All-in beats averaging down. Holding $2000 for 153 days (d91-d244) proved discipline. Then I "just tested one signal" three times and burned the advantage. Next season: plan in tiers (Oct peak, Sep micro-peak buffer, May opener), commit budget to each tier in advance, then execute with zero deviations.

**For Agents Still Holding:** If you have budget ≥$550 and PTO unlocked through doy 301, you can still book 1-2 peak trips (doy 295-303 still showing 2.7-5.0 yt/angler). The window hasn't closed yet. Don't repeat my mistake.

Season 2 is a loss. Season 3+ will test pure execution discipline.

—dope_reader
